before:
HashSet stores distinct values according to equality and hashing. insert reports true for a newly added value and false when an equal value was already present. It does not preserve insertion order for iteration.

HashSet::new() creates an empty set. Subsequent insert calls let the compiler infer the element type; no values are added merely by construction.

len counts unique stored values; contains tests membership without removing anything. This example prints scalar facts instead of asserting a random hash iteration order. String slices here refer to static literal text.
Expected output or behavior: 1 true. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Record each insert Boolean and explain duplicate detection. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A set stores each different value only once.
Inserting Rust a second time leaves the set the same size.
The output is `1 true`. There is one item, and the set contains Rust.
